Commentary.Commentary: Curtains down on this series - And with that, it's time to wrap things up from this game and the series as well. Pakistan take the honours with a 2-1 victory, and the trophy is now in the hands of skipper Shaheen Afridi, who joins his teammates in lifting it aloft and posing for pictures behind the Winner’s banner. Australia's next assignment is just around the corner as they travel to Bangladesh for a three-match ODI series starting on June 9, while Pakistan take a short break before switching their focus to red-ball cricket, with two Tests against West Indies in the Caribbean, beginning on July 25. There's plenty of cricket happening elsewhere too, with England taking on New Zealand in the Crowe-Thorpe Trophy and West Indies locking horns with Sri Lanka in ODI cricket, among several other contests around the world. Until next time, cheers and goodbye!

The captain of Australia -  Josh Inglis starts off saying that they were too many runs short, just like the first game of the series. However, he brings the spotlight on the effort of bowlers and the fielding group to put themselves in a position where they could win the game but it just didn't work for them. Inglis mentions that the young players have performed well for the side and he is happy about it. About their upcoming series in Bangladesh, he says that the team will surely try to rectify their mistakes and would like to get better results in Bangladesh.

PLAYER OF THE SERIES - The youngster, Arafat Minhas, who made his ODI debut in this series, wins the award for his all-round effort. He made 60 runs and picked up 7 wickets in 3 matches. Minhas says that he is happy with the series win, and he is happy with the team's enthusiasm. He adds that they always prepare with a positive mindset, and that is very important. Arafat shares that this is a good platform to gain confidence and ends by saying that they will keep on giving their best always.

PLAYER OF THE MATCH - The victorious skipper of Pakistan, Shaheen Afridi, wins the award for his excellent bowling spell of 3/30(8). Afridi says that it was a team effort throughout the series. Adds that it was a difficult track for the batters, and their batters did really well. He says that they need to adapt to the conditions and it was a great series. Shaheen reckons that they were happy to restrict Australia to a low total and the credit goes to their bowlers. He ends by saying that he always keeps on giving his best, and the rest follows.
Presentation Time...

Australia's bowlers show fight despite defeat - Australia should be proud of the way they bowled, but to be honest, they just did not have enough runs on the board. Nathan Ellis set the tone with an early wicket, while Matthew Short followed to push the hosts onto the back foot. However, it was Matthew Kuhnemann who spun a web around the batters with a fantastic three-wicket haul, including the big wicket of Babar, which gave them a glimmer of hope and could have been more damaging had a few close calls gone his way, otherwise, the result might have been even tighter. Adam Zampa went wicketless despite being economical, but he needed breakthroughs to give Australia a better chance in this decider.

Inglis fights a lone battle - Earlier in the game, Australia were bowled out for a meagre 157 in this series decider, losing their last seven wickets for just 38 runs. Only skipper Josh Inglis offered any real resistance with a gritty 65 off 71 balls, but beyond that, it was a sorry-looking scorecard, with as many as seven batters falling in single digits and no one else even crossing 20, which says it all. Pakistan were all over the Aussies, with skipper Shaheen Afridi leading from the front with a fine three-wicket haul. Abrar Ahmed and Shadab Khan picked up a couple each, while Haris Rauf chipped in with one, and a couple of run-outs capped off an all-round effort in the field.

Men in Green overcome pressure to get home - Pakistan made a steady start to the chase, but Sahibzada Farhan's brief stay halted early momentum. Maaz Sadaqat showed intent with a few fluent strokes, yet he couldn't convert his start into a meaningful score. Through the innings, Babar Azam held things together with calm authority in testing, slow conditions, anchoring one end while wickets continued to tumble around him. Just as he looked set to guide Pakistan closer, he too fell to a delivery that had his name written all over it, his 40 off 84 balls taking the chase deep but still leaving work to be done. With pressure mounting, Abdul Samad and Shadab Khan rose to the occasion, showing great composure to stitch together a crucial unbeaten 49-run stand and finish the job in style.

Pakistan continue ODI dominance over Aussies - Pakistan make it a hat-trick of 2-1 ODI series wins over Australia, one away and two at home. Chasing what looked like a modest target at the break, it would have been easy to expect a walk in the park for the Men in Green. However, Australia pushed them all the way with a spirited fight, showing real character to take the hosts deep and giving themselves plenty to be proud of despite falling short. And with that, the wait for Australia to win an ODI series in Pakistan since 1998 continues.

FOUR! Shadab Khan finishes off in style. Pakistan had to wait a little longer to celebrate, but it's all happy faces in their dugout. Short of a length, on off, Shadab Khan hangs back and swats it over the mid on region for four runs. Pakistan beat Australia by four wickets and win the series 2-1.

Commentary.Commentary: Appeal for LBW, but turned down! Flighted, full and on off, turns in sharply, Maaz Sadaqat steps across to defend on the front foot but misses and gets hit on the pads. Clearly, impact is outside off here and the Aussies do not take the review.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Matthew Kuhnemann to Maaz Sadaqat, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Gets it away! Floated, full and around off, Maaz Sadaqat leans onto his drive, plays it right under his eyes and carasses it through covers for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Matthew Kuhnemann to Maaz Sadaqat, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up, full and on middle, Maaz Sadaqat fends it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Matthew Kuhnemann to Maaz Sadaqat, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter, full and on off, Maaz Sadaqat jams it off the bottom end of the bat towards short mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Matthew Kuhnemann to Maaz Sadaqat, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: This is exactly what Australia needed. Babar Azam comes out to bat now. Also, Matthew Kuhnemann comes into the attack for the Aussies.

OUT! BOWLED'EM! Nathan Ellis works his magic yet again and gets the first breakthrough. He rolls his fingers to bowl the fast off-cutter and executes it to perfection, on off, grips, and moves in sharply. Sahibzada Farhan fails to read it and tries to punch it away from the crease without any footwork. He leaves a big gap between bat and pad and the ball goes through to rattle the stumps. Farhan is not happy with himself, but has to walk back cheaply here. Pakistan are 27/1, chasing 158 runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Nathan Ellis to Sahibzada Farhan, OUT! b Nathan Ellis.

Commentary.Commentary: Pulls his length back a bit, on off, Maaz Sadaqat opens the bat face and guides it towards deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Nathan Ellis to Maaz Sadaqat, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Fine shot! Very full and on middle and off, Maaz Sadaqat gets right underneath the ball. He hits it through the line, thumping it over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Nathan Ellis to Maaz Sadaqat, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Another slower delivery, full and on middle and leg, Maaz Sadaqat keeps it out to the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Nathan Ellis to Maaz Sadaqat, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pace off, on a length and on off, Maaz Sadaqat blocks it out solidly.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Nathan Ellis to Maaz Sadaqat, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and on middle, angling in, Sahibzada Farhan clips it away with good timing wide of mid on. Alex Carey chases after it and slides to push it back inside to save a run. Three taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Nathan Ellis to Sahibzada Farhan, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Slight halt! Maaz Sadaqat takes a blow to his helmet, and the physio is having a check at it. All good to continue.

FOUR LEG BYES! Cameron Green bangs in a quick bouncer, on middle. Maaz Sadaqat looks to pull it away but gets hurried and misses. The ball bangs on the top of the helmet and flies to the third man fence for another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Cameron Green to Maaz Sadaqat, 4 Leg byes.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! That's right from the middle of the bat! Fuller delivery and around off, Maaz Sadaqat gets his hands through the shot and creams it through covers for a boundary. This should give him some confidence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Cameron Green to Maaz Sadaqat, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length and around off, at 141.5 kph, holds its line. Maaz Sadaqat withdraws his bat at the last moment and lets it go to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Cameron Green to Maaz Sadaqat, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Lands this on a good length and on middle, angling in sharply, Maaz Sadaqat fails to flick it away but misses and gets hit high on the pads. A slight appeal for LBW, but turned down. Probably going down the leg side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Cameron Green to Maaz Sadaqat, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length and just outside off, angles in, Maaz Sadaqat goes chasing after it but gets another inside edge towards fine leg for a couple of runs. He is yet find the middle of the bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Cameron Green to Maaz Sadaqat, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and around off, Sahibzada Farhan opens the bat face and guides it to deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Cameron Green to Sahibzada Farhan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Cameron Green begins with a full delivery but down the leg side, Sahibzada Farhan fails to glance it away. Wided.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Cameron Green to Sahibzada Farhan, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Who will bowl from the other end? Cameron Green it is!

FOUR! Streaky! Nathan Ellis hits the length hard and on off, gets it to nip back in a bit. Maaz Sadaqat stays back and tries to push it away but gets very late on the shot. The ball catches the inside edge and flies past the stumps and to the fine leg fence for the first boundary of the chase.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Nathan Ellis to Maaz Sadaqat, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Another slower one, full and on middle, Sahibzada Farhan clips it to deep square leg for another run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Nathan Ellis to Sahibzada Farhan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and around off, Sahibzada Farhan cuts it on the bounce to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Nathan Ellis to Sahibzada Farhan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Goes fuller and on middle, hint of shape in, Maaz Sadaqat looks to play at it but gets an inside edge towards square leg for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Nathan Ellis to Maaz Sadaqat, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pakistan are underway in the chase! Pace off from Ellis, back of a length and on off, Sahibzada Farhan punches it wide of mid off for a single. He turns back for the second but Marnus Labuschagne is quick to get to the ball and releases it quickly to the bowler's end. Seeing that, Maaz sends his partner back just in time.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Nathan Ellis to Sahibzada Farhan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nathan Ellis starts with a full delivery, on middle, holds up in the surface a bit. Sahibzada Farhan drives it a bit uppishly but safely towards mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Nathan Ellis to Sahibzada Farhan, No run.
